value: germination of Satureja thymbra seeds was 12.4% in the water control, 34.4% after the Pinus brutia smoke solution (letter b, differs from control) and 24.3% after the Quercus infectoria smoke solution (letter ab, between control and P); the Chrysopogon gryllus solution was not tested for lack of seeds (one-way ANOVA F 7.77, P 0.0102); mean time to reach 50% germination did not change (t50 15.0, 13.0, 11.6 days; P 0.5378)
method: seeds sown on agar in Petri dishes after a 24 h soak in water (control, Cont) or in an aqueous smoke solution made by heating 5 g of dry Pinus brutia (P), Quercus infectoria subsp. boissieri (Q) or Chrysopogon gryllus subsp. gryllus (Ch) material for 30 min at 190-195 C and adding 50 mL distilled water; germination counted for 35 days
conditions: 20 +/- 1 C in darkness; 4 replicate dishes of 25 seeds (100 seeds per treatment); ripe fruits collected from at least 10 individuals in burned areas of the Marmaris region, south-western Turkey, in August 2010 and stored in paper envelopes at room conditions; no heat pretreatment of seeds; Table 2 gives mean germination % (G) with SE in parentheses, one-way ANOVA at alpha 0.05 (F, P), letters mark groups that differ; all species except Lavandula stoechas had control germination below 12.5%; the smoke solutions were from three different plants and did not differ from one another in effect on germination percentage or rate; in the same paper Sarcopoterium spinosum (control 11.0%, 32.0/26.0/25.0% in P/Q/Ch) and Satureja thymbra rose, while Calicotome villosa, Cistus salviifolius and Lavandula stoechas did not; Ch was not tested for this species because of limited seed; t50 row 15.0 (3.2), 13.0 (1.4), 11.6 (1.1), F 0.67, P 0.5378; post-hoc test Tukey HSD; seeds stored 7.5 months before testing; no smoke-solution dilution reported and dish size not stated

value: germination of Calicotome villosa seeds was 8.3% in the water control, 6.7% after the Pinus brutia smoke solution and 16.1% after the Quercus infectoria smoke solution, with no significant difference among groups (one-way ANOVA F 1.19, P 0.3475; null); the Chrysopogon gryllus solution was not tested
method: seeds sown on agar in Petri dishes after a 24 h soak in water (control, Cont) or in an aqueous smoke solution made by heating 5 g of dry Pinus brutia (P), Quercus infectoria subsp. boissieri (Q) or Chrysopogon gryllus subsp. gryllus (Ch) material for 30 min at 190-195 C and adding 50 mL distilled water; germination counted for 35 days
conditions: 20 +/- 1 C in darkness; 4 replicate dishes of 25 seeds (100 seeds per treatment); ripe fruits collected from at least 10 individuals in burned areas of the Marmaris region, south-western Turkey, in August 2010 and stored in paper envelopes at room conditions; no heat pretreatment of seeds; Table 2 gives mean germination % (G) with SE in parentheses, one-way ANOVA at alpha 0.05 (F, P), letters mark groups that differ; all species except Lavandula stoechas had control germination below 12.5%; the smoke solutions were from three different plants and did not differ from one another in effect on germination percentage or rate; in the same paper Sarcopoterium spinosum (control 11.0%, 32.0/26.0/25.0% in P/Q/Ch) and Satureja thymbra rose, while Calicotome villosa, Cistus salviifolius and Lavandula stoechas did not; Ch was not tested for this species because of limited seed; the 16.1% under Q carries SE 7.3 and no letter, so the paper counts it as no change; t50 row 4.7 (1.3), 6.0 (3.1), 4.2 (0.4), F 0.01, P 0.9930; control germination was low (8.3%); the authors attribute the lack of response in C. villosa (and Cistus salviifolius) to physical dormancy imposed by hard seed coats; seeds were not scarified or heat-treated, so this null is for intact hard-coated seed and does not show insensitivity to smoke; post-hoc test Tukey HSD; seeds stored 7.5 months before testing; no smoke-solution dilution reported and dish size not stated

value: germination of Lavandula stoechas seeds was 81.0% in the water control and 93.1%, 90.6% and 89.3% after the Pinus brutia, Quercus infectoria and Chrysopogon gryllus smoke solutions, a rise the paper calls obvious but nonsignificant (one-way ANOVA F 1.76, P 0.2076; null)
method: seeds sown on agar in Petri dishes after a 24 h soak in water (control, Cont) or in an aqueous smoke solution made by heating 5 g of dry Pinus brutia (P), Quercus infectoria subsp. boissieri (Q) or Chrysopogon gryllus subsp. gryllus (Ch) material for 30 min at 190-195 C and adding 50 mL distilled water; germination counted for 35 days
conditions: 20 +/- 1 C in darkness; 4 replicate dishes of 25 seeds (100 seeds per treatment); ripe fruits collected from at least 10 individuals in burned areas of the Marmaris region, south-western Turkey, in August 2010 and stored in paper envelopes at room conditions; no heat pretreatment of seeds; Table 2 gives mean germination % (G) with SE in parentheses, one-way ANOVA at alpha 0.05 (F, P), letters mark groups that differ; all species except Lavandula stoechas had control germination below 12.5%; the smoke solutions were from three different plants and did not differ from one another in effect on germination percentage or rate; in the same paper Sarcopoterium spinosum (control 11.0%, 32.0/26.0/25.0% in P/Q/Ch) and Satureja thymbra rose, while Calicotome villosa, Cistus salviifolius and Lavandula stoechas did not; the authors attribute the null to loss of seed dormancy after 7.5 months of seed storage (81% control germination) and note that earlier studies (Keeley and Baer-Keeley 1999; Moreira et al. 2010, 2012) found smoke- and charred-wood-stimulated germination in L. stoechas; this null is for after-ripened seed (the paper contrasts it with the other four species, whose controls were below 12.5%); t50 row 3.1 ab (0.3), 2.9 ab (0.5), 2.1 a (0.1), 3.9 b (0.5), F 3.94, P 0.0360, so germination rate differed only between Q and Ch smoke solutions and not against the control; post-hoc test Tukey HSD; seeds stored 7.5 months before testing; no smoke-solution dilution reported and dish size not stated
